To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ERP response to BIAT faking is differentially affected by ego depletion.
depletion of self-control resources did not influence the ability to fake the BIAT, but did influence the brain response to the BIAT.
faking a BIAT evokes a characteristic EEG response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to detect faked responses in implicit psychological tests and can be used for future detection and prevention strategies.
the question of whether the brain activity that underlies faking on the Brief Implicit Association Test is modulated by temporarily available self-control.
a better understanding of the cerebral processes that underlie faking on a brief implicit association task and its potential use as a tool for the detection of deception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain processes of faking are more complex than previously assumed and that the brain processes are not directly linked to the overt faking behavior.
self-control resources are not necessary to successfully fake a test, but that the brain activity involved in this process is different when self-control resources are depleted.
self-control resources are important in the cerebral processes underlying deception but not in the behavioral outcome of the test.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is not a reliable indicator for faking, as the brain does not always show the same pattern when faking.
depletion of self-control resources does not affect the overt faking success, however, the brain activity during BIAT is significantly different between the two conditions.
self-control resources play no role in the overt faking success of the BIAT but they do influence the underlying cerebral processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BIAT is a promising tool for the detection of deception.
the ERP response to BIAT faking is not a reliable marker for the detection of faking.
faking is not necessarily an all-or-nothing phenomenon.
